subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: What retry budget and retryable-error classifier should the shared OAuth refresh path use, and should provider-plugin refresh hooks be wrapped by the same policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but auth-provider retry semantics are compatibility-sensitive because they affect permanent auth failures, provider-plugin behavior, and the existing hard timeout/lock path.

options.title: Bounded shared retry with classifier
options.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh owner path with a narrow transient-error classifier, focused tests, and no retry for terminal OAuth failures.

options.title: Provider-owned retry only
options.body: Leave core single-shot and require each provider or provider plugin to implement its own retry semantics where safe.

options.title: Keep single-shot behavior
options.body: Accept transient refresh failures as terminal until the user retries or restarts, preserving today’s simplest auth semantics.

recommendation.title: Bounded shared retry with classifier
recommendation.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh owner path with a narrow transient-error classifier, focused tests, and no retry for terminal OAuth failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc authored the current OAuth lifecycle manager extraction and recent adjacent auth hardening work, making him the strongest routing candidate for the retry policy choice.
